To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the energy-momentum tensors of the pions, kaons, and etas are not traceless in the limit of zero quark masses.
the trace of the energy-momentun tensor is a dilatation current, the dilatation current is a scalar density, the scalar density is a dilataton, and the dilatation is a dilaton current.

the divergence of the energy-moment tensor is a sum of two terms: the first term is a sum of the divergence of the dilatation current, plus terms involving the scalar meson nonet and the second term involves the scalar meson tenth term.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the algebraic structure and physical content of the energy-moment tensor in Lagrangian quantum field theories.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence that the I = 1/2 K-meson is a bound state of two pions.
the Gell-Mamm-Oakes-Rennew symmetry breaking mechanism is not a symmetry breaking of the algebra of the energy-momentun tensor, but a symmetry breaking of its trace.
the scalar mesons are not a part of the nonet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trace θ is a good candidate to contain a piece proportional to the I = 1 scalar meson.
the I = 1, 2 scalar mesons, if they exist, must have masses less than 1.2 GeV.
the I = 1 scalar mesons are the most important source of the divergences in the trace of the energy-moment tensor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dilatation current is not the divergence of a vector current in the presence of scalar mesons.
the trace θ of Tμν is not just a “dilatation-like” current but a “dilaton” current, and that the “dilaton”, as a composite object, is not just a scalar but a “scalar meson”.
the scalar mesons are not only the source of the trace anomaly but are the source of the dilatation current.
